description: This topic covers first aid, first aid kits, common accidents and their treatment, safety in the laboratory and at home, basic rescue and resuscitation, and how to prevent accidents.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of the term 'first aid'?

options.text: The complete medical treatment given by a doctor in a hospital
The immediate help given to an injured or sick person before professional help arrives
The money paid to a patient after an accident
The act of taking a sick person to a traditional healer

mcq.explanation: First aid is the initial assistance given to a casualty before a doctor or ambulance arrives, to save life and prevent the condition from getting worse.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is one of the main aims of first aid?

options.text: To preserve life, prevent the condition from worsening and promote recovery
To replace the work of doctors permanently
To collect blood samples for testing
To perform surgery on the casualty

mcq.explanation: The three main aims of first aid are to preserve life, prevent the situation from becoming worse, and promote recovery of the casualty.

mcq.questionText: Which item below is normally found in a first aid kit?

options.text: A mobile phone charger
Cotton wool and bandages
A kitchen knife
A bottle of soda

mcq.explanation: A first aid kit contains items such as cotton wool, bandages, plasters, antiseptic, scissors and gloves used to treat minor injuries.

mcq.questionText: A student in the laboratory spills a strong acid on her hand. What is the correct first aid action?

options.text: Rub the hand with a dry cloth
Wash the area with plenty of running water immediately
Cover the hand and ignore it
Apply cooking oil to the hand

mcq.explanation: Acid on the skin should be washed off immediately with plenty of running water to dilute and remove the acid and reduce burning.

mcq.questionText: What is the first thing you should do to a person who has fainted?

options.text: Give them food to eat
Lay them down and raise their legs slightly to improve blood flow to the brain
Make them stand up quickly
Pour cold water into their mouth

mcq.explanation: Fainting is caused by reduced blood flow to the brain; laying the person down and raising the legs helps blood return to the brain.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the correct first aid for a minor cut that is bleeding?

options.text: Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth and raise the part if possible
Pour soil on the wound to stop bleeding
Leave the wound open in the dust
Squeeze more blood out of the wound

mcq.explanation: Applying direct pressure with a clean cloth and raising the injured part helps to stop the bleeding and reduce blood loss.

mcq.questionText: What does CPR stand for in first aid?

options.text: Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation
Care Patient Recovery
Cold Pressure Relief
Continuous Pain Removal

mcq.explanation: CPR stands for Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation, a technique combining chest compressions and rescue breaths to help a person whose heart and breathing have stopped.

mcq.questionText: Which laboratory rule helps to prevent accidents from chemicals?

options.text: Tasting chemicals to identify them
Never eating, drinking or tasting chemicals in the laboratory
Mixing any chemicals to see what happens
Working without telling the teacher

mcq.explanation: Eating, drinking or tasting chemicals can cause poisoning, so it is strictly forbidden in the laboratory.

mcq.questionText: A person is bitten by a snake while working on a farm in a village. Which of the following is the correct first aid?

options.text: Let the person run quickly to spread the venom faster
Keep the person calm and still, immobilise the limb and rush them to hospital
Cut the wound deeply with a knife
Give the person a lot of alcohol to drink

mcq.explanation: Keeping the casualty calm and the bitten limb still slows the spread of venom, and getting them quickly to hospital for anti-venom is essential.

mcq.questionText: Why should a first aid kit be kept in a clean, dry and easily reachable place?

options.text: So that it looks attractive in the room
So that supplies stay clean and can be used quickly during an emergency
So that children can play with it
So that it can be sold easily

mcq.explanation: A clean, dry and accessible location keeps the materials sterile and allows quick use when an accident happens.

mcq.questionText: What is the correct first aid for a small burn caused by hot water (scald)?

options.text: Apply toothpaste and cover tightly
Cool the burn under clean running water for several minutes
Burst any blisters that form
Rub the area with salt

mcq.explanation: Cooling a burn with clean running water reduces the heat and pain and limits the damage to the skin; blisters should not be burst.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the best way to prevent accidents at home?

options.text: Storing medicines and paraffin where children can reach them
Keeping sharp objects, chemicals and electrical wires safely and out of reach of children
Leaving the floor wet and slippery
Playing with fire near curtains

mcq.explanation: Storing dangerous items safely and out of children's reach prevents many common home accidents such as poisoning, cuts and electric shocks.

mcq.questionText: A person has received an electric shock and is still touching the live wire. What should you do FIRST?

options.text: Grab the person with your bare hands immediately
Switch off the power source before touching the person
Pour water on the person
Run away and leave the person

mcq.explanation: Switching off the power first protects the rescuer from also being electrocuted; never touch a victim still in contact with electricity.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a common cause of poisoning at home in Tanzania?

options.text: Drinking clean boiled water
Swallowing paraffin (kerosene) or pesticides stored in soda bottles
Eating fresh fruits
Breathing fresh air

mcq.explanation: Storing paraffin or pesticides in soft drink bottles often causes accidental poisoning, especially among children who mistake them for drinks.

mcq.questionText: When trying to rescue a drowning person, what is the safest action for an untrained rescuer?

options.text: Jump into deep water immediately even if you cannot swim
Reach out with a stick, rope or float and pull the person to safety
Watch the person without doing anything
Throw stones at the person

mcq.explanation: An untrained rescuer should reach or throw a stick, rope or floating object rather than entering the water, to avoid drowning together with the victim.

fib.questionText: The immediate help given to an injured person before professional medical help arrives is called _____.
fib.explanation: First aid is the first assistance given to a casualty to preserve life and prevent the condition from worsening.

fib.questionText: A box or container holding materials such as bandages, plasters and antiseptic for treating injuries is called a first aid _____.
fib.explanation: A first aid kit holds the supplies needed to give first aid during an emergency.

fib.questionText: The person who gives first aid to a casualty is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A first aider is a person trained to give first aid to someone who is injured or suddenly ill.

fib.questionText: An injured or sick person who needs first aid is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A casualty (or victim) is the person who has been injured or taken ill and requires help.

fib.questionText: A liquid used to clean a wound and kill germs to prevent infection is called an _____.
fib.explanation: Antiseptics such as iodine or dettol clean wounds and destroy microorganisms that could cause infection.

fib.questionText: Loss of consciousness for a short time caused by reduced blood flow to the brain is called _____.
fib.explanation: Fainting happens when the brain temporarily receives too little blood; laying the person down helps recovery.

fib.questionText: The emergency technique that combines chest compressions and rescue breaths to restart breathing and heartbeat is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Resuscitation, such as CPR, is used to revive a casualty whose breathing or heartbeat has stopped.

fib.questionText: Bleeding from a cut should be controlled by applying direct _____ on the wound with a clean cloth.
fib.explanation: Applying pressure on the wound helps the blood to clot and stops further bleeding.

fib.questionText: In the laboratory, you should always wear a _____ to protect your clothes and body from chemicals.
fib.explanation: A laboratory coat (lab coat) protects the body and clothing from spills of chemicals and other hazards.

fib.questionText: Taking action to stop accidents from happening, such as keeping floors dry and storing chemicals safely, is called accident _____.
fib.explanation: Accident prevention means removing hazards and following safety rules so that accidents do not occur.

tf.questionText: First aid is meant to replace the treatment given by a doctor in hospital.
tf.explanation: First aid is only the immediate temporary help; the casualty should still be taken to a doctor or hospital for full treatment.

tf.questionText: One of the aims of first aid is to preserve the life of the casualty.
tf.explanation: Preserving life is one of the three main aims of first aid, together with preventing the condition from worsening and promoting recovery.

tf.questionText: A first aid kit should be kept in a damp and dusty place.
tf.explanation: A first aid kit must be kept clean, dry and easily reachable so the materials remain sterile and ready for use.

tf.questionText: Acid spilled on the skin should be washed off with plenty of running water immediately.
tf.explanation: Washing with plenty of water dilutes and removes the acid quickly, reducing burns to the skin.

tf.questionText: It is safe to taste chemicals in the laboratory to find out what they are.
tf.explanation: Tasting chemicals can cause serious poisoning and is strictly forbidden in the laboratory.

tf.questionText: When someone faints, you should make them stand up and walk around quickly.
tf.explanation: A fainted person should be laid down with the legs raised to help blood return to the brain, not forced to stand.

tf.questionText: Before touching a person who is still in contact with a live electric wire, you must first switch off the power.
tf.explanation: Switching off the power first prevents the rescuer from also receiving an electric shock.

tf.questionText: Storing paraffin or pesticides in used soda bottles is a safe practice at home.
tf.explanation: Storing poisons in drink bottles often leads to accidental poisoning, especially among children.

tf.questionText: An untrained person should jump into deep water to rescue a drowning person.
tf.explanation: An untrained rescuer should reach or throw a stick, rope or float instead of entering deep water, to avoid drowning too.

tf.questionText: Wearing protective clothing and keeping the floor dry are ways of preventing accidents.
tf.explanation: Protective clothing and dry floors reduce hazards and help to prevent injuries at home, at school and in the laboratory.

summary.correctAnswer: First aid is the immediate help given to an injured or sick person before professional medical help arrives.
summary.explanation: It is temporary care meant to save life and prevent the condition from getting worse.

summary.questionText: The three main aims of first aid
summary.correctAnswer: To preserve life, to prevent the condition from becoming worse, and to promote recovery.
summary.explanation: These aims guide every first aider when helping a casualty.

summary.questionText: Examples of items in a first aid kit
summary.correctAnswer: Bandages, plasters, cotton wool, antiseptic, scissors, gloves and a pair of forceps.
summary.explanation: These supplies are used to clean and dress wounds and treat minor injuries.

summary.correctAnswer: Apply direct pressure on the wound with a clean cloth and raise the injured part.
summary.explanation: Pressure and raising the part help to stop the bleeding and reduce blood loss.

summary.questionText: First aid for burns and scalds
summary.correctAnswer: Cool the burn with clean running water for several minutes and do not burst any blisters.
summary.explanation: Cooling reduces pain and skin damage; bursting blisters increases the risk of infection.

summary.correctAnswer: Lay the person down, raise the legs, and allow fresh air to reach them.
summary.explanation: This helps blood flow back to the brain so the person regains consciousness.

summary.correctAnswer: Resuscitation is the action of reviving a person whose breathing or heartbeat has stopped, for example using CPR.
summary.explanation: CPR combines chest compressions and rescue breaths to restart the heart and breathing.

summary.correctAnswer: Never eat, drink or taste chemicals, wear protective clothing, and follow the teacher's instructions.
summary.explanation: These rules protect students from poisoning, burns and other laboratory accidents.

summary.correctAnswer: Cuts, burns, falls, poisoning, electric shocks and drowning.
summary.explanation: Knowing common accidents helps people to prevent them and give correct first aid.

summary.correctAnswer: Keep floors dry, store chemicals and sharp objects safely out of reach, and follow safety rules.
summary.explanation: Removing hazards and obeying safety rules greatly reduces the chance of accidents.

hoq.questionText: During a chemistry practical at school, a student suddenly knocks over a beaker and gets a deep cut that bleeds heavily on the arm. As the first aider, which sequence of actions is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Wash the cut with chemicals from the bench, then continue the experiment
Apply firm direct pressure with a clean cloth, raise the arm, then take the student to hospital
Tell the student to shake the arm to remove the blood
Pour soil into the wound and bandage it

hoq.explanation: Direct pressure and raising the arm control heavy bleeding, and the deep cut then needs professional treatment at hospital.

hoq.questionText: A young child at home swallows paraffin that was kept in a soda bottle. Which is the BEST first aid response?

options.text: Force the child to vomit immediately
Keep the child calm, do not force vomiting, and rush them to hospital with the paraffin container
Give the child a lot of soap to drink
Wait and see if the child becomes sick before acting

hoq.explanation: Vomiting paraffin can damage the lungs if inhaled, so the child should be taken quickly to hospital with the container to help doctors identify the poison.

hoq.questionText: You find a person lying near a river who is not breathing after being pulled from the water. Trained help is far away. Why is starting resuscitation quickly so important?

options.text: Because the brain can be damaged within minutes if it does not receive oxygen
Because resuscitation makes the person warmer
Because it is required by law to look busy
Because it dries the person's clothes

hoq.explanation: Without oxygen the brain begins to suffer permanent damage within a few minutes, so resuscitation must start as soon as possible to keep oxygen reaching the brain.
